scope: Franchise lineage events for the 32 current NFL franchises, seasons 1970-2025 (1969 used as the baseline)

kinds.merger_realignment: 1970: placed into the AFC or NFC and a new division by the AFL-NFL merger
kinds.expansion: first season of a new franchise
kinds.new_franchise: first season of a franchise that is legally new but took over another club's organisation (Ravens 1996)
kinds.relocation: home city changed (name city changes with it)
kinds.rename: name changed without a move (nickname, or geographic name for the same home)
kinds.suspension: franchise did not play from this season
kinds.reactivation: suspended franchise resumed play this season

conventions.season: the first season the change applies to
conventions.from/to: identity for the season before / the season of the event (null when there was none)
conventions.identities: consecutive seasons with the same city, name, conference and division (from PFR season standings)
conventions.abbreviation: project display convention, not a historical claim

season_summary_note: teams, games (most played by any team), playoff_teams (teams PFR marks as division winner or wild card) and division names, computed from the PFR season standings

league_events.note: AFL-NFL merger in effect: 26 teams in the AFC and NFC, three divisions each; Baltimore, Cleveland and Pittsburgh joined the 10 former AFL teams in the AFC.
Playoff home field by record replaces the 1970-1974 divisional rotation.
Seattle and Tampa Bay join: 28 teams.
Regular season 14 -> 16 games; second wild card per conference (10 playoff teams) with a Wild Card round.
Players' strike: 9-game regular season (PFR records); 16-team playoff tournament, top eight per conference regardless of division (Wikipedia cross-check).
Players' strike: 15-game regular season (PFR records; one week cancelled, three weeks played by replacement players - replacement detail: Wikipedia cross-check).
Third wild card per conference: 12 playoff teams.
Cleveland franchise suspended 1996-1998; Baltimore Ravens begin. Still 30 teams.
Houston Texans join (32 teams); eight four-team divisions (AFC/NFC East, North, South, West); playoffs: four division winners and two wild cards per conference.
Playoffs expand to 14 teams (seven per conference, one bye each); approved March 31, 2020.
